documents_expected.why: initiative page: grant size, scope, eligible applicants, deadline
Guidelines for Applicants with corrigenda: eligibility, costs, required documents, deadline

eligibility.rule: Research institutions, CSOs, NGOs or government bodies active on invasive species management in the EU
eligibility.quote: be either a research institution, a Civil Society Organization (CSO 1), a Nongovernmental Organisation (NGO) or government or government-affiliated entity active on the management of IAS in the EU.

eligibility.rule: Bank account in the organisation's name; allowed to receive charitable contributions
eligibility.quote: have a bank account in the name of the organisation; be authorized under relevant national laws to receive charitable contributions, including from sources outside their respective countries.

eligibility.rule: Project in an EU country (overseas territories only Canaries, Azores, Madeira); lead based in an eligible country
eligibility.quote: Projects must be implemented in countries of the European Union. The only eligible European Union overseas countries and territories are the Canary Islands, the Azores and Madeira.
alt_quotes: The lead contact and their organisation must be based in an eligible country.

eligibility.rule: Early-stage invasion of an alien plant or animal with high risk of spread
eligibility.quote: The project must directly address an early-stage invasion of an alien species (i.e. nonnative) (either breeding or non-breeding) that has a high risk of spread in the near future
The projects must incorporate physical eradication measures of an IAS.

eligibility.rule: Proven capacity to implement the activities
eligibility.quote: The applicant must demonstrate proven capacity to implement the proposed activities and identify and adopt any relevant best practices as well as innovative methods for eradication.

eligibility.rule: €10,000–€50,000, up to 12 months; indirect costs at most 7%; no land, firearms or sub-grants
eligibility.quote: Indirect costs are eligible up to 7% of the estimated total eligible direct costs.

documents.item: Online application in the IUCN Grants Portal (project, logframe, ESMS, budget, due diligence)
documents.quote: Applications can be submitted only through the IUCN GRANTS PORTAL.
Articles of Incorporation, Constitution, Statutes, Government Decree, as appropriate (certificate of registration or bylaws)
Location map (shapefile or digital map - see note on shapefiles at the end of this section)
CVs of key project staff (short CVs preferred)
Confirmation letters from your partners (if applicable) can be submitted in the "Additional Documents" section.
Please submit evidence of the invasiveness (e.g. survey results, research, project results etc.).

effort.step: Submit the proposal in the IUCN Grants Portal (rolling; closes earlier if funds run out)
effort.quote: The current deadline to submit proposals for Invasive Alien Species Rapid-Response Funds under this call is 10 February 2027 at 14:00 (2pm) Central European Time (CET).
alt_quotes: Call status: Open - application deadline: 10 February 2027, 14:00 (CEST)

consortium_required.quote: The Lead Partner may act individually or with partner(s).

after_award.quote: Frequency of reporting Reporting period (cumulatively in the final report)

notes: Projects starting from October 2026 must end by 30 September 2027 (corrigendum 2). Mandatory monitoring indicators are reported per reporting period and in the final report; the schedule is set in the grant agreement. The guidelines live on the IUCN Grants Portal (a JavaScript app; the PDF loads from speciesgrantsapi.iucn.org when you click 'Guidelines for Applicants' on the call card). The initiative page says 14:00 CEST; the guidelines say 14:00 CET.
